candidates.decision_relevance: The reviews repeatedly describe rebounds, renewed weakness, and differing short- and long-window returns, but often lack aligned underlying hourly BTC and ETH prices. Historical hourly paths would let researchers reconstruct the sequence and compare it with ETH/BTC without relying on endpoint summaries.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11 cite partial or unavailable short-window samples and unresolved path ordering; weekly reviews W37–W45 also note missing granular price paths.
candidates.metric_name: Hourly BTC and ETH reference-price observations with observation timestamps
candidates.missing_history_problem: Without a consistent historical path, the timing, magnitude, and persistence of rebounds and drawdowns cannot be checked against the point-in-time observations discussed in the reviews.

candidates.decision_relevance: Breadth is repeatedly described as proxy-only, with changing membership between captures and no canonical broad-alt or large-cap series. Historical constituent-level observations under a stable, documented universe would clarify whether participation broadened or narrowed independently of aggregate price endpoints.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews 2026-11-09 through 2026-11-11 report changing top-100 membership and proxy breadth; W37–W45 reviews identify missing breadth paths, construction, or comparable observations.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped constituent returns and advancer/decliner membership for a consistently defined breadth universe
candidates.missing_history_problem: Point-in-time proxy counts with different membership hashes do not establish a comparable participation trend or whether breadth changes preceded or followed price weakness.

candidates.decision_relevance: Several daily reviews have only one settled ETF session or a stale row, while weekly reviews explicitly warn against carrying prior-week flows forward. A dated history of settled BTC and ETH ETF flow observations would permit comparison across the same periods as price and breadth.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews 2026-11-09 through 2026-11-11 report last-settled rows dated November 6 or a single November 9 session; W44–W45 reviews note absent week-specific settled-flow detail.
candidates.metric_name: Dated settled BTC and ETH ETF flow totals, with units and covered session
candidates.missing_history_problem: Sparse or stale settlement rows cannot establish whether flows persisted, changed direction, or coincided with the reviewed price and participation sequences.

candidates.decision_relevance: The daily reviews mention liquidation aggregates as lower bounds from a fragile source and state that historical backfill is unavailable. If timestamped observations with coverage/completeness metadata can be retained, they could help assess whether liquidation episodes preceded or followed the price moves rather than treating snapshots as persistent evidence.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews 2026-11-09 through 2026-11-11 describe lower-bound liquidation aggregates, unverified completeness, and unavailable historical backfill.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped liquidation observations with source coverage and completeness metadata
candidates.missing_history_problem: Current or rolling lower-bound aggregates without a reliable historical sequence cannot support timing comparisons or distinguish an isolated observation from persistent activity.
